source.title: Leverage Is Not Reach: A Control-Window Law for Single-Neuron Steering in Language Models

page_placements.theme: Training origins: harm discrimination predates alignment; post-training creates or amplifies a refusal gate shaped by the objective
Measurement of refusal and bypass depends on scorer, decoding and serving setup

record.tranche_reason: The study uses a different intervention from the original: it doses individual FFN-neuron write directions and measures refusal bypass and actionable content, rather than finding and ablating the harmful-minus-harmless residual-stream direction.
record.gate_note: The refusal results test single-neuron interventions and their behavioral outcomes. Values cited from other studies are not recorded as results here. The paper also reports many benign steering examples and discovery-screen comparisons; they are not included unless they bear on a listed claim version.
record.test_reason: The study doses individual FFN-neuron write directions (W_down columns) and measures refusal bypass and actionable content. It never computes, ablates or adds the harmful-minus-harmless difference-in-means direction. Its only contact with that direction is as a readout tool: neuron-write cosines with the refusal axis (Sec. 8) and a refusal-projection readout (App. B.3). Its results concern single-neuron controllability, not whether any version holds. Bypass vs. actionable content is an output-content distinction, not a separately encoded harmfulness judgment (V5). The base-to-instruct comparison concerns neuron write columns, not the refusal direction (V6/V7).
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct but misses the main thesis. The paper's central claim is a control-window law: coherent single-neuron control exists when a behaviour trigger lies below a collapse ceiling set by the coherence budget. The refusal results use the law as a measurement tool, showing coherent bypass and strict-actionable reach separate (genuine reach on 3 of 6 Llama pivots, committing late in the rollout). The base-to-instruct appendix is offered as an interpretation, not an established mechanism. The authors also say single-neuron pivots lie off the Arditi refusal axis and flip it by propagation.
record.recipe_differences: The original studies a difference-in-means residual-stream direction and removes or adds it across layers and positions. This paper screens individual FFN neurons contrastively and doses their down-projection write directions; it does not directly intervene on the original refusal direction.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported outcome depends on calibrated dose and rollout horizon; coherent bypass and strict-actionable content are judged separately. The paper reports that actionable content commits later in the rollout than bypass.

fits_no_version.finding: Single-neuron coherent refusal bypass (0.29–0.96, n=24) is decoupled from strict-actionable content (0.00–0.88) across six Llama-3.1-8B pivots.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Behavioural refusal bypass from a single-neuron intervention does not imply actionable harmful content.

fits_no_version.finding: Safety neuron write columns are largely preserved from base to instruct in Qwen, while their harmful-vs-benign activation gap is amplified 4× to 1650×. Llama L11/F4258 is rewritten instead.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Alignment training gates refusal by amplifying pre-existing neuron-level harm-discriminative signals.

fits_no_version.finding: Confirmed safety neurons write off the refusal readout direction (cosine 0.04 for L12/F4593, 0.02 for L8/F397, within the random band). The authors say they flip refusal by downstream propagation.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Components that causally control refusal need not write along the refusal direction.

fits_no_version.finding: Safety and arithmetic pivot directions fall within the random-pair cosine band (44/45 pairs).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Single-neuron behaviour gates for different behaviours occupy near-orthogonal directions.

record.problems: The base-to-instruct comparison is not a controlled intervention on training and has selected pivots. Refusal evidence uses small audited request sets (n = 24 for the cohort); several per-pivot rates have no stated interval. The study does not test the original difference-in-means direction, all-layer ablation, harmless-request false refusals, or broad capability preservation.
record.rows_left_out: Omitted the 15-neuron prospective ceiling-validation summary and the many benign routing/operator examples because they measure the control-window framework rather than the refusal-direction versions; also omitted cited prior-study outcomes.

untested.parts: All: no difference-in-means direction is computed, ablated or added; no capability-preservation test for such a direction.
All: no weight-edit/abliteration; stated as future work.
All: no jailbreak or adversarial-training analysis.
All: no affine, cone or multi-direction comparison.
All: no representation of harmfulness judgment is probed separately from the refusal decision.
All: no transfer of the refusal direction across languages, variants or base-to-instruct.
All: no test of whether training yields a single removable refusal direction.

record.verdict_notes: The reader linked neuron-level results to V1/V5/V6/V7 by analogy. None measures the difference-in-means refusal direction or its transfer or ablation, so all rows are unlinked and no verdicts are given. The refusal-axis cosine result (Sec. 8) is the closest contact with the claim and has no row; it is listed under fits_no_version.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test the harmful-minus-harmless difference-in-means residual direction, projection from every layer and position, adding that direction on harmless requests, or broad preservation of other abilities. Tests calibrated interventions along individual neuron write directions and refusal behavior on the audited requests.
No weight-edit/abliteration experiment; direct weight-edit validation is described as future work.
Does not test whether jailbreak attacks suppress the difference-in-means direction or whether training against its ablation improves robustness.
Does not compare affine, cone, or multi-direction accounts of the refusal direction. Its cross-sector cosine result is for safety versus arithmetic pivots, not the geometry among refusal directions.
Tests coherent refusal bypass versus strict-actionable content on the audited cohort; does not establish a general representational location or mechanism for harmfulness judgments.

Tests base-to-instruct transfer for selected neuron write directions and associated signals, not transfer of the harmful-minus-harmless mean direction across languages or broadly across model variants.
Uses a base-to-instruct comparison; does not intervene on the training process or vary when, how, or with what data refusal training occurs.

unmatched_labels.reason: No row measures what any version names. Bypass vs. actionable content is about the output, not V5's internal harm encoding. Base-to-instruct results concern neuron columns and activation gaps, not transfer of the direction (V6) or one removable direction (V7).

relation.reason: A refusal readout axis is used for cosine and projection measurements, but no result bears on whether that direction mediates refusal. 'discusses' would be the next-closest call.

tranche.reason: The study doses single FFN-neuron write columns. It never computes, ablates or adds the difference-in-means direction. Its only contact with a refusal direction is as a readout: neuron-write cosines with the 'refusal readout direction' (0.04 for L12/F4593, 0.02 for L8/F397) and a refusal-projection readout in Appendix B.3. Its 'sharpens Arditi' remark (Discussion; Table 6) says pivots flip the axis 'by propagation', which is compatible with V1 and not measured, so it is not T5.

source_check.notes: The text never says how the 'refusal readout direction' (Section 8) is built. Only Table 6 ties it to Arditi's difference-of-means axis. Single-author preprint (Palo Alto Networks), no code. Per-pivot doses and horizons are said to be in Appendix D.1 but are not given there in the text.

statements.problem: None. 4x and 1650x are the Table 14 values for the two Qwen2.5-3B pivots, at weight cosine 1.0000 and above 0.998. L11/F4258 is 'rewritten (top 0.15% in layer)'.

statements.correction: Coherent bypass (Claude-Haiku, n=24): L16/F6950 0.62, L15/F9635 0.62, L17/F13532 0.29, L10/F1084 0.96. L10/F4789 and L11/F4258: figure only, at least their 0.88 actionable rate (text: strict-actionable is the lowest rate for every pivot). Strict-actionable peak: 0.00, 0.17, 0.00, 0.75, 0.88, 0.88.
statements.problem: The 0.29-0.96 bypass range is presented as covering six pivots, but the text states bypass numbers for only four of them (0.62, 0.62, 0.29, 0.96). L10/F4789 and L11/F4258 bypass appears only in Figure 7. The actionable range 0.00-0.88 over six pivots and n=24 are correct.
